name: Red Fort
desc: Massive red sandstone walls that once ran an empire. Walk where emperors schemed, then exit straight into Old Delhi's snack gauntlet.

name: India Gate
desc: A war memorial arch with lawns where half of Delhi turns up for evening ice cream. Free, floodlit, iconic.

name: Qutub Minar
desc: A 73-metre victory tower from 1193 still out-flexing every skyscraper on style. The carved ruins around it are the bonus level.

name: Humayun's Tomb
desc: The garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal — quieter, redder, closer. Golden hour here feels illegal at this price.

name: Lotus Temple
desc: A giant marble lotus where everyone's welcome and it costs nothing. The silence inside hits different after Delhi traffic.

name: Chandni Chowk
desc: A 400-year-old market maze — jalebi stands, paratha lanes, rickshaws playing bumper cars. Bring an appetite, not a plan.

name: Lodhi Gardens
desc: Crumbling 15th-century tombs scattered through jogger-filled gardens. Picnic among dynasties for exactly zero rupees.

name: Jama Masjid
desc: One of India's grandest mosques — climb a minaret and Old Delhi unrolls beneath you like a map. Entry free, views priceless.

name: Akshardham Temple
desc: A carved sandstone mega-temple so detailed it doesn't look real. Free to enter, impossible to fit on a postcard.

name: Hauz Khas Complex
desc: Medieval fort ruins on a lake, right beside boutique cafés — study the 14th century, then people-watch the 21st. Free.
